title: Ordered systolic blood-pressure curvature does not improve transported classification of low FEV1/FVC in two NHANES cycles
abstract: We tested whether the signed curvature SBP1−2SBP2+SBP3 from three routine pressure readings improves classification of prebronchodilator FEV1/FVC<0.70 beyond average pressure, systolic variability and linear trend, demographics, anthropometry and smoking. Models trained in NHANES2007–2008 (3361 adults; 472 cases) were frozen and evaluated in separately recruited NHANES2011–2012 (3333; 409 cases). Target weighted Brier score worsened from 0.09801441 to 0.09889924, delta +0.00088483; joint rescaled-PSU bootstrap95% interval [-0.00006365,+0.00332694]. Incremental benefit was not established. This is an exploratory temporal-transport negative result, not equivalence, evidence of causal harm, or a COPD diagnostic study. Shared survey protocols and prior data exposure limit confirmation.
